raw.markdown:
# TESE / Micro-TESE — Authorization Guide
Subtitle: CPT Codes · ICD-10 · Payer Requirements
backHref: /tese

## CPT Codes

| CPT | Description | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 54500 | Biopsy of testis, needle (separate procedure) | Diagnostic |
| 54505 | Biopsy of testis, incisional (separate procedure) | Diagnostic/TESE |
| 54512 | Excision of extraparenchymal lesion of testis | Surgical |
| 54520 | Orchiectomy, simple (not used for TESE but related) | Related |
| 89264 | Sperm identification from testis tissue, fresh or cryopreserved | Lab — sperm ID |
| 89337 | Cryopreservation, sperm | Cryopreservation |
| 89352 | Thawing of cryopreserved; sperm/semen | Thaw for IVF |
| 58321 | Artificial insemination; intra-uterine | Related ART |

Note: Micro-TESE is typically billed as 54505 (incisional testis biopsy). Some payers recognize 54512. Always verify with individual payer policy.

## ICD-10 Diagnoses

| ICD-10 | Description |
| --- | --- |
| N46.01 | Organic azoospermia |
| N46.021 | Azoospermia due to obstructive causes |
| N46.029 | Azoospermia due to other obstructive causes |
| N46.11 | Organic oligospermia |
| Q98.0 | Klinefelter syndrome with karyotype 47,XXY |
| Q98.4 | Klinefelter syndrome, unspecified |
| Q96.9 | Turner syndrome, unspecified (female partner) |
| Z31.41 | Encounter for fertility testing |
| Z31.81 | Encounter for male factor infertility in female patient |
| C62.90 | Malignant neoplasm of testis, unspecified (oncofertility) |

## Coverage Landscape

### Common Denial Reasons
- "Infertility treatment" blanket exclusion
- "Experimental" claim for micro-TESE (incorrect — well-established since 1999)
- Sperm cryopreservation (89337) denied as "storage"
- Lab code 89264 denied as "not medically necessary"

### Strongest Coverage Arguments
- Azoospermia is a diagnosable medical condition (N46.01), not merely infertility
- Micro-TESE is standard of care per AUA/ASRM — not experimental
- Oncofertility: ASCO guidelines mandate fertility preservation counseling before gonadotoxic therapy
- State infertility mandates cover diagnostic and surgical procedures
- Klinefelter syndrome (Q98.0) is a chromosomal disorder — coverage may fall under genetic/chromosomal benefit

## Prior Authorization Requirements

### Required Documentation
- ≥2 semen analyses confirming azoospermia (performed ≥4 weeks apart)
- Hormonal profile: FSH, LH, total testosterone, inhibin B
- Scrotal ultrasound
- Karyotype and Y-chromosome microdeletion analysis
- CFTR mutation testing (if CBAVD suspected)
- Testicular biopsy report (if available)
- Letter of medical necessity from fellowship-trained urologist/andrologist
- For oncofertility: oncology treatment plan documenting gonadotoxic therapy

### Medical Necessity Criteria
- Confirmed azoospermia on ≥2 semen analyses
- Hormonal and genetic evaluation completed
- No absolute contraindication (complete AZFa/AZFb deletion)
- Microsurgical expertise available (fellowship-trained andrologist)
- Female partner evaluation completed or oncofertility indication
